extracted.intended_audience: students, researchers, and practitioners in public relations, communications, media studies, and political/strategic communication
extracted.subtask_description: A broad reference for recognizing and classifying propaganda: its defining features, source-based types, transmission strategies, and a comprehensive list of common techniques used to shape perceptions, emotions, attitudes, and behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: propaganda as deliberate systematic persuasion
rubrics_metrics.description: "Propaganda is the deliberate, systematic attempt to shape perceptions, manipulate cognitions, and direct behavior to achieve a response that furthers the desired intent of the propagandist."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on intent (to shape perceptions/behavior), systematic application, and targeted audiences; distinguishes propaganda from neutral information provision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: propaganda as one-sided, controlled messages
rubrics_metrics.description: "A systematic form of purposeful persuasion that attempts to influence the emotions, attitudes, opinions, and actions of specified target audiences ... through the controlled transmission of one-sided messages (which may or may not be factual) via mass and direct media channels."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key markers: one-sidedness, control of transmission, possible factual inaccuracy or selective facts; look for restrictions on countervailing information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Propaganda characteristic: appeal to emotion not intellect
rubrics_metrics.description: "Propaganda is generally an appeal to emotion, not intellect."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Messages designed to provoke emotional responses (fear, pride, anger, euphoria) rather than reasoned argument are a hallmark; watch for emotive language and imagery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Propaganda characteristic: selective presentation / lying by omission
rubrics_metrics.description: "Propaganda often presents facts selectively (thus possibly lying by omission) ... uses loaded messages to produce an emotional rather than rational response."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate completeness: omitted context, cherry-picked facts, and absence of counter-evidence indicate propagandistic framing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of repetition / ad nauseam
rubrics_metrics.description: "Ad nauseam — uses tireless repetition of an idea. An idea... repeated enough times may begin to be taken as the truth."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for repeated slogans, images, jingles, or assertions across channels and over time; repetition amplifies perceived truth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification by source: white, black, and grey propaganda
rubrics_metrics.description: "White propaganda generally comes from an openly identified source... Black propaganda is identified as being from one source, but is in fact from another... Grey propaganda is propaganda without any identifiable source or author."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess source transparency and authenticity. White = overt, identifiable; grey = anonymous/ambiguous; black = false attribution or covert origins.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strategic transmission pattern / indoctrination stages
rubrics_metrics.description: "Propaganda campaigns often follow a strategic transmission pattern ... begin with a simple transmission ... contain directions on how to obtain more information ... initiate the individual from information recipient to information seeker through reinforcement, and then from information seeker to opinion leader through indoctrination."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Watch for staged pathways: initial exposure, reinforcement, calls-to-action, mechanisms to convert consumers into advocates/opinion leaders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Media and channel indicators
rubrics_metrics.description: "Common media for transmitting propaganda messages include news reports, government reports, historical revision, junk science, books, leaflets, movies, radio, television, and posters ..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Propaganda can appear in any medium; assess format (news-like content, advertorials, PSAs, documentaries) and whether it mimics objective formats to increase credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technique: ad hominem
rubrics_metrics.description: "Ad hominem — attacking one's opponent, as opposed to attacking their arguments."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Spot personal attacks that substitute for substantive rebuttal; these undermine rational debate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technique: appeal to authority
rubrics_metrics.description: "Appeals to authority cite prominent figures to support a position, idea, argument, or course of action."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check whether authority is relevant/expert and whether the appeal substitutes for evidence; misuse of celebrity or irrelevant experts is common.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technique: appeal to fear
rubrics_metrics.description: "Appeal to fear — seeks to build support by instilling anxieties and panic in the general population."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify messages that emphasize danger, threat, or catastrophe to push policy or behavior changes; assess plausibility and evidence for the threat.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technique: appeal to prejudice (loaded/emotive terms)
rubrics_metrics.description: "Using loaded or emotive terms to attach value or moral goodness to believing the proposition. Used in biased or misleading ways."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for language designed to trigger pre-existing biases or moral reactions rather than reasoned evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technique: bandwagon / join the crowd
rubrics_metrics.description: "Bandwagon and 'inevitable-victory' appeals attempt to persuade the target audience to join in and take the course of action that 'everyone else is taking'."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Messages that emphasize majority behavior or inevitability to induce conformity should be treated skeptically; inspect evidence for claimed majority support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technique: beautiful people
rubrics_metrics.description: "Depicts attractive, happy people to imply that buying or following will make you happy or successful."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize aspirational imagery that links emotional benefit to adherence rather than providing substantive justification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technique: the lie / big lie
rubrics_metrics.description: "The repeated articulation of a complex of events that justify subsequent action... 'big lie' generalizations merge and eventually supplant the public's accurate perception."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Watch for large, repeated false narratives that simplify complex events and are reiterated across channels to overwrite factual perceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technique: black-and-white fallacy
rubrics_metrics.description: "Presenting only two choices, with the product or idea being propagated as the better choice. For example: 'You're either with us, or against us.'"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beware forced dichotomies that exclude nuance and alternative solutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technique: classical conditioning
rubrics_metrics.description: "If object A is always present when object B is present and object B causes a physical reaction ... then when presented with object A ... we will experience the same feelings."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify pairing of symbols/images with emotional stimuli; positive or negative feelings transfer to associated messages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technique: cognitive dissonance exploitation
rubrics_metrics.description: "People desire to be consistent... use endorsements or associations to force reconciling inconsistent attitudes and change beliefs."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for engineered inconsistencies exploited to shift opinions (e.g., celebrity endorsement to shift attitudes about a candidate/product).

rubrics_metrics.name: Technique: common man / plain folks
rubrics_metrics.description: "Attempts to convince the audience that the propagandist's positions reflect the common sense of the people by communicating in the common manner and style of the target audience."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check for staged 'everyday' language or behaviors used to create affinity; verify authenticity of 'plain folks' portrayals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technique: cult of personality
rubrics_metrics.description: "Creates an idealized and heroic public image of an individual through mass media and unquestioning flattery."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note disproportionate praise and personalization of messages; look for centralization of legitimacy in a single charismatic figure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technique: demonizing the enemy / dehumanization
rubrics_metrics.description: "Making individuals from the opposing nation/ethnic group appear subhuman, worthless, or immoral."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify language/images that dehumanize and justify hostile policy or violence toward the target group.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technique: dictat (directive imagery)
rubrics_metrics.description: "Uses images and words to tell the audience exactly what actions to take, eliminating any other possible choices (e.g., 'I want you')."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Spot content that issues commands or prescriptive directives framed as singular correct actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technique: disinformation
rubrics_metrics.description: "The creation or deletion of information from public records, in the purpose of making a false record of an event ... including outright forgery of photographs, motion pictures, broadcasts, and sound recordings as well as printed documents."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify provenance of documents/media; look for doctored or fabricated evidence intended to mislead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technique: door-in-the-face
rubrics_metrics.description: "Used to increase a person's latitude of acceptance by making an extreme first request, then retreating to a smaller target request."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detect staged escalation/retreat patterns designed to make an intermediate ask seem reasonable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technique: euphoria (mood manipulation)
rubrics_metrics.description: "Use of an event that generates euphoria or happiness, or using an appealing event to boost morale (declaring holidays, parades, making luxury items available)."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether positive events are being leveraged instrumentally to increase support or distract from issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technique: fear, uncertainty, and doubt (FUD)
rubrics_metrics.description: "An attempt to influence public perception by disseminating negative and dubious/false information designed to undermine the credibility of their beliefs."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Spot campaigns that emphasize ambiguity and sow distrust to paralyze decision-making or erode competitors' credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technique: flag-waving / patriotism appeals
rubrics_metrics.description: "Attempts to justify an action on the grounds that doing so will make one more patriotic or benefit a country/group the target audience supports."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scrutinize patriotic symbolism used to short-circuit critical assessment of policies or actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technique: foot-in-the-door
rubrics_metrics.description: "Starts with a small favor/gift to create obligation, then requests a larger favor later."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify incremental compliance strategies that exploit social reciprocity to obtain larger commitments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technique: glittering generalities
rubrics_metrics.description: "Emotionally appealing words applied to a product or idea, but present no concrete argument or analysis (PT Barnum effect)."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beware vague praise and grandiose claims lacking measurable specifics or evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technique: half-truth
rubrics_metrics.description: "A deceptive statement that includes some element of truth—partly true, or true but only part of the whole truth."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cross-check claims against fuller context; partial truths often conceal critical qualifiers or counter-evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technique: labeling (euphemism/dysphemism)
rubrics_metrics.description: "Using labels to increase perceived quality (euphemism) or to discredit (dysphemism); creating categories to uplift or defame without direct legal defamation."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyze how naming frames perceptions (e.g., 'liberal' as a dysphemism) and whether labels are applied inconsistently to manipulate sentiment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technique: latitudes of acceptance manipulation
rubrics_metrics.description: "Two techniques: take an extreme position to make moderate ones seem acceptable, or moderate one's own position then slowly move it further over time."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Watch for deliberate repositioning or use of extreme anchors to shift norms and acceptability over time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technique: love bombing
rubrics_metrics.description: "Recruit by isolating a person from social support and bombarding them with affection to replace prior beliefs with the group's."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In recruitment or cult contexts, identify intense, orchestrated displays of affection used to detach recruits from previous networks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technique: lying and deception (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: "Many propaganda techniques are based on dishonesty or deception, including outright stretching or breaking the truth."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat unverified sensational claims with skepticism; check primary sources and corroborating evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technique: managing the news / staying on message
rubrics_metrics.description: "Confine itself to a few points and repeat them over and over ... 'Staying on Message.'"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track message discipline across spokespeople and media; repetition of a small set of talking points signals coordinated messaging.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technique: milieu control
rubrics_metrics.description: "Attempt to control the social environment and ideas through the use of social pressure."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Observe social coercion, ostracism, or information-control mechanisms in networks and communities restricting dissent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technique: name-calling
rubrics_metrics.description: "Use of pejorative names to incite fears and arouse prejudices, intended to provoke conclusions apart from impartial examination of facts."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify derogatory labels employed to delegitimize opponents rather than engaging their arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technique: obfuscation / intentional vagueness / confusion
rubrics_metrics.description: "Generalities are deliberately vague so that the audience may supply its own interpretations ... the intention is to cause people to draw their own interpretations rather than being presented with an explicit idea."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flag deliberately vague claims that avoid testable specifics and encourage passive acceptance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technique: obtain disapproval / Reductio ad Hitlerum
rubrics_metrics.description: "Persuade a target audience to disapprove of an action by suggesting that the idea is popular with groups hated or feared by the audience."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be wary of guilt-by-association tactics that link ideas to disreputable groups to discredit them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technique: operant conditioning
rubrics_metrics.description: "Involves learning through imitation; watching an appealing person endorse positions teaches a person to buy the product or endorse the position."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Spot modeled behavior and endorsements used to normalize actions via social learning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technique: oversimplification / favorable generalities
rubrics_metrics.description: "Favorable generalities are used to provide simple answers to complex problems."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Challenge simplistic solutions presented for complex social, political, or economic issues and demand evidence and nuance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technique: pensée unique (enforced reduction of discussion)
rubrics_metrics.description: "Enforced reduction of discussion by use of overly simplistic phrases or arguments (e.g., 'There is no alternative to war.')."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detect rhetorical closure that excludes alternatives and narrows public debate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technique: quotes out of context
rubrics_metrics.description: "Selectively editing quotes to change meanings—used to discredit opponents or opposing viewpoints."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify original sources of quoted material and assess whether editing changes intended meaning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technique: rationalization (making excuses)
rubrics_metrics.description: "Use favorable generalities to rationalize questionable acts or beliefs, using vague pleasant phrases to justify them."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify justifications framed in value-laden but evidence-poor language that normalize questionable conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technique: red herring
rubrics_metrics.description: "Presenting data or issues that, while compelling, are irrelevant to the argument at hand, and then claiming that it validates the argument."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish between relevant evidence and distracting information used to divert attention from core issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technique: scapegoating
rubrics_metrics.description: "Assigning blame to an individual or group to alleviate feelings of guilt from responsible parties and/or distract attention from the need to fix the problem."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note when complex problems are reduced to blame on a single target without systemic analysis or accountability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technique: slogans
rubrics_metrics.description: "A brief, striking phrase that may include labeling and stereotyping; tends to act only as emotional appeals."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate slogans for factual content and whether they replace reasoned argument with emotional shorthand.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technique: stereotyping
rubrics_metrics.description: "Attempts to arouse prejudices by labeling the object of the campaign as something the target audience fears or hates; often focuses on anecdote rather than representative data."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scrutinize anecdotal evidence and portrayals that generalize traits to entire groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technique: straw man
rubrics_metrics.description: "Creating a misrepresented position of an opponent and refuting the weaker straw man rather than the original proposition."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare summarized opponents' positions with their actual statements; exposing misrepresentation undermines the attack.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technique: testimonial
rubrics_metrics.description: "Quotations, in or out of context, especially cited to support or reject a policy—reputation/role of the individual is exploited."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess the expertise and independence of testimonial sources and whether they are used as proxy evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technique: third party technique / astroturfing
rubrics_metrics.description: "People are more willing to accept an argument from a seemingly independent source than from someone with a stake in the outcome; includes hiring journalists, front groups, or using scientists within the organization to present prejudicial findings."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigate funding, affiliations, and independence of apparent third-party endorsers; look for coordinated front organizations or astroturf campaigns.
